title: Former Redlands Deputy Chief Earns $1.26 Million in 2025 While on Leave, Amid Retaliation and Misconduct Allegations
text:
A former Redlands police deputy chief received $1.26 million in total compensation in 2025, the highest among California city employees, while on paid administrative leave. The payout was part of a retirement settlement linked to his retaliation claim after reporting misconduct, including sexual harassment allegations and evidence concealment in a fatal crash.
A former Redlands police deputy chief, Travis Martinez, earned approximately $1.26 million in total compensation in 2025, the highest amount reported for any city employee in California , despite not having worked a single day that year.
This substantial payout, which includes $81,804 in regular pay, $890,467 in other pay, and $231,099 in lump-sum compensation, was part of a settlement agreement upon his retirement in April. The city also contributed $55,864 toward retirement and health benefits. Martinez had been on paid administrative leave for about 18 months before retiring.
His compensation exceeded that of other high-earning municipal employees, such as a Los Angeles Fire Department battalion chief who earned over $921,000 and a Los Angeles Department of Water and Power supervisor who earned more than $779,000. The State Controller's Office publishes annual salary data for California's public employees, but the database does not identify individuals by name. Transparent California linked the 2025 compensation to Martinez.
Martinez's lucrative exit was tied to a legal claim he filed in 2023, alleging retaliation by city officials after he reported misconduct within the police department. In his claim, he stated he raised concerns about attempts to conceal evidence related to a deadly crash that killed a Redlands woman and her 11-year-old daughter. He also reported allegations of sexual misconduct involving former Deputy Chief Mike Reiss to the FBI, believing internal handling was inadequate.
As part of the settlement, Martinez agreed to retire and dismiss his claim in exchange for a payment reported to total roughly $872,000. His claim highlighted an "exemplary" 29-year career and alleged he was repeatedly passed over for promotion because he refused to ignore misconduct. Retaliation allegations against the Redlands Police Department extend beyond Martinez. Former Deputy Chief Mike Reiss retired in March 2023 after accusations that he groomed, sexually harassed, and preyed on several department employees over years.
Former Police Chief Chris Catren also retired days earlier, citing a work-related injury and denying any connection to the controversy. Over the past three years, Redlands has approved more than $3.3 million in settlements to resolve sexual harassment lawsuits tied to Reiss. The most recent settlement, approved in June, was for $475,000 with former forensic specialist Geneva Holzer, who agreed to resign and dismiss her lawsuit.
These cases reveal significant institutional turmoil and costly legal resolutions stemming from internal misconduct and the handling of whistleblower complaints within the Redlands Police Department
